proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently runs one way only, so we have added the Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct, and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.

ops.newText: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
ops.oldText: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice and reasonable cooperation, and the indemnifying Party controls the defence and settlement, provided no settlement imposes an obligation on the indemnified Party without its consent.

proposal.summary: Add a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and narrow the Customer indemnity.

quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
rationale: Section 20 contains only a broad one-way Customer indemnity and no Vendor IP or misconduct indemnity anywhere in the document (Section 9.3 even cross-refers to non-existent Section 20.5 remedies), which is walk-away territory. We added the Vendor indemnity with standard procedure and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law.

rationale: We own Customer Data and Deliverables with a Vendor assignment, Vendor retains only Vendor Technology subject to the perpetual licence in Section 13.2, and Section 14.4 rules out joint ownership. Preferred position met.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A one-month cap applied "without exception" is far below our floor of 12 months' fees and would swallow the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3, so we have reset the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 and restored the carve-out. Indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches sit outside the cap.

ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.

proposal.summary: Make the cap the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1M and preserve the Excluded Claims carve-outs.

quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
rationale: The cap is mutual and Sections 21.2–21.3 contain the exclusion of indirect damages, the full Excluded Claims carve-out list and the payment-obligations carve-out. However, one month of Fees actually paid is well below the 6-month walk-away floor, and "without exception" purports to override the Excluded Claims. We reset the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 and restored the carve-out.

rationale: We have an affiliate/successor assignment right without consent, Vendor needs our consent (never to a competitor), and Section 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, suspension or repricing on our change of control. Preferred position met.

ops.oldText: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.

proposal.summary: Extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocability at will.

quote: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
rationale: The Services grant is revocable at Vendor's discretion and expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them — walk-away territory — even though Sections 13.2 and 13.3 provide better terms for paid-up software and transfers. We extended the grant to Affiliates and contractors and limited revocation to the Section 13.3 uncured-breach standard.

rationale: A 24-month post-term restriction of undefined scope in any territory is walk-away, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3; we have deleted it.

ops.newText: On expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition, export, and migration assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates, and shall not delete Customer Data except as provided in Sections 11.2 and 11.3.
ops.oldText: Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.

proposal.summary: Replace immediate deletion with up to six months' transition assistance before deletion.

quote: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
rationale: Sections 11.2 and 11.3 give 30-day data return and certified deletion, but Section 11.1 mandates immediate deletion with no export or migration help, which is walk-away and contradicts them. Replaced with up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, with deletion sequenced after return.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A fifteen-day warranty that then cuts off all correction and refund obligations is below our floor, so we have moved to ninety days and kept the re-perform/repair/replace or refund remedy in Section 19.4.

ops.newText: For ninety days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation, and Vendor shall provide the remedies in Section 19.4 for any nonconformity Customer reports during that period.
ops.oldText: For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.

proposal.summary: Extend the Deliverable conformance warranty to 90 days with the Section 19.4 remedy preserved.

quote: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
rationale: Sections 19.1, 19.3 and 19.4 give a strong workmanlike/compliance/no-malicious-code warranty with real remedies and a disclaimer that does not swallow them, but the 15-day conformance period with a hard cut-off on correction and refund obligations falls below the 90-day/30-day fallback. Extended to ninety days with the Section 19.4 remedy preserved.
